plain: A nuclear explosion, even a very large one, would not meaningfully change Earth's rotation, because even the biggest nuclear weapons ever tested release energy that is astronomically small compared to the energy involved in Earth's rotational momentum. The largest nuclear weapon ever detonated, the Soviet Tsar Bomba, released around 50 megatons of energy, but Earth's rotational kinetic energy is on the order of 10^29 joules, making even that massive explosion utterly negligible by comparison. Even a hypothetical arsenal of every nuclear weapon on Earth detonated simultaneously would still fall enormously short of having any measurable effect on the planet spinning on its axis. For comparison, even massive earthquakes only change the length of a day by fractions of a microsecond, illustrating just how much energy would actually be required.

plain: Taveuni, known as the 'Garden Island' of Fiji, offers several great activities for visitors. First, snorkeling or diving the Rainbow Reef is a must, considered one of the best soft coral diving sites in the world. Second, hiking to the Bouma Waterfalls within Bouma National Heritage Park lets you swim in three separate stunning waterfall pools connected by jungle trails. Third, visiting the Waitavala Water Slide offers a fun, natural rock water slide formed by a river. Fourth, exploring Lavena Coastal Walk provides stunning ocean views combined with lush rainforest scenery. Fifth, visiting the International Date Line, which runs through Taveuni, lets you stand with one foot in today and one in yesterday, a quirky photo opportunity unique to the island.
